rule: A monster is one data row: fixed level, uniform HP roll in a range, damage range, up to three strikes each with its own range and a reflex-gated hit chance, armour as row value times five, a metal gate that zeroes damage from weaker weapons, weight that drives knockback (closed form 40 damage squared over weight plus 10 damage, floor 15), frame rates per action, and a strike-frame marker (-1) in the attack sequence where damage applies. A variant is the same row with a different skin, move sound and glow; the golem family is four rows with identical numbers. Class enemies follow the player's level; city watch add 3 to 6 levels. Idle, bark and attack sounds run on timers and coin flips on the client (3-9 s bark timer within 16 units, 80/20 bark versus step, attack sound half the time).

data_fields.name: monster.weight
data_fields.unit: classic weight units; 0 means no monster knockback

keep: Monster as one data row with fixed level and ranges.
Uniform HP roll in the row range at spawn.
Strike-frame marker (-1) in the attack sequence that applies damage.
Metal gate that zeroes damage from weaker weapons.
Golem-family pattern: same numbers, four skins, one glow.
Bark and step cadence on a random timer; attack sound about half the time.
change: One server random stream for every roll (the reflex check uses the classic generator and the damage roll uses the Unity generator, FormulaHelper.cs:657 and :659).
Write the knockback closed form directly (the 256 fixed-point factor cancels, EnemyAttack.cs:343-344).
Metal-gate feedback as a rune flash and sound, not a text popup (FormulaHelper.cs:580).
Validate at load that rows used by spawns have fields; the placeholder row 39 is empty (EnemyBasics.cs:1561).
Our names, numbers and skins; donor values are reference only.
Cap strikes per swing at three and tie the cap to the MAX_ATTACKERS constant.
look_test: Target src/fight/creature-family.ts (proposed), parity row 7. One strike clip with a -1 strike frame shown on three skins of one row (plain, tinted, glowing; same numbers). A 2-second loop per skin. On the strike frame a short rune flash plays before the damage number. Show one weapon below the metal gate: rune flash, no damage, no text popup. Dom checks: the three skins read as one family at 375 wide in a still; the rune flash lands before the damage number; the no-effect gate reads as blocked without a text line. Pass if the first two hold; if the third fails, keep the flash and drop the sound.
